title: Digital business and labour: incentives, opportunities and power

slides.title: Digital systems change how organizations work
lines: Transactions create records for operations
Shared tools can coordinate people across places
Platform rules can distribute access to customers
slides.notes: The economic context examines how people work and exchange goods and services. A business uses digital systems to coordinate employees, record transactions and understand demand. A platform can also decide which seller or creator a customer encounters. We will connect a system’s mechanism to opportunities and constraints for different people. A successful business outcome does not automatically mean every worker or customer benefits. This deck covers the assigned business and working-practice sections, and identifies the remainder of the economic chapter.
slides.prompt: Name one decision a business can make using transaction records.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 213.
slides.alt: Teaching diagram: Digital systems change how organizations work. Its relationships are explained in the visible transcript.

slides.title: Operation and organization of a business
lines: Shared calendars and files can coordinate a team
Databases and transaction systems record activity
Data analysis can support stock, staffing or service decisions
slides.notes: Consider a school event shop. Each sale updates a transaction record. Summing sales by item can inform the next stock order. A shared calendar helps volunteers coordinate, and a shared document records decisions. The system connects information to action. The textbook describes movement towards more dynamic teams, but that is a possible organizational change rather than a universal outcome of using software. A company can adopt digital tools while retaining a strict hierarchy. Explain the specific change in the example you use.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 213–214.

slides.title: Customer value and business incentives
lines: An organization may trade immediate profit for repeat use
Advertising, subscriptions and commissions reward different outcomes
The revenue model can influence what a system optimizes
slides.notes: A subscription service may value renewal, a marketplace may earn a commission on completed sales, and an advertising-funded service may gain from opportunities to show ads. These are possible incentives, not proof of the objective used by every business. A platform’s ranking choice can support one of those outcomes. Distinguish a claim about the business model from evidence about an actual ranking rule. Consider customer value, operating costs and other constraints as well as revenue.
slides.prompt: Which evidence would connect a revenue model to a specific ranking choice?
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 213–214.
slides.alt: Teaching diagram: Customer value and business incentives. Its relationships are explained in the visible transcript.

slides.title: Transaction data becomes a decision
lines: An invented event shop records 12 badge sales and 4 poster sales
A stock decision can use those totals
The decision also needs context: stock, price and who attended
slides.notes: These numbers are invented. Badges may have sold more because they were cheaper or available for longer. A manager might order more badges, but should check whether the poster stock ran out or whether a different audience will attend next time. The mechanism is transaction capture, aggregation, interpretation and a stock decision. The implication is conditional: if the pattern continues and the stock decision matches demand, waste may fall. Avoid turning a single descriptive total into a guaranteed forecast.
table: Did price or stock limit purchases?

options: Guaranteed demand at the next event
The only reason customers chose badges
quiz.why: A total supports a description. Prediction and cause require more context.

slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 213–214.

slides.title: Diversification and workforce diversity
lines: Diversification changes products, markets or the supply chain
Workforce diversity concerns the people in an organization
Inclusion concerns whether people can participate and feel respected
slides.notes: The chapter uses diversity in two related but different senses. A business may diversify what it sells, and it may seek a diverse workforce. These should not be confused. An inclusive organization also examines whether people can participate effectively, rather than simply counting demographic categories. Digital recruitment can broaden access, but an unsuitable screening rule can exclude applicants. The next two slides explain the textbook’s four diversification categories using invented examples, before we return to hiring and power.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 214–215.

slides.title: Horizontal and vertical diversification
lines: Horizontal: add a complementary product or service
Vertical: take over another part of the supply or production chain
Classify the relationship, not merely the fact that a company grows
slides.notes: Using the textbook’s terminology, a video platform adding a messaging service is horizontal diversification because it offers a complementary service. An online seller operating its own delivery fleet is vertical diversification because it takes over a part of its supply or delivery chain. These are invented illustrations. A firm can pursue more than one strategy, so explain which relationship a particular decision changes. Avoid memorizing a company name as if it always belongs to one category.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 214.

slides.title: Concentric and conglomerate diversification
lines: Concentric: adapt an existing line for a wider audience
Conglomerate: enter an unrelated product or industry
The distinction follows the textbook’s definitions
slides.notes: A platform adapting its existing service for business accounts illustrates concentric diversification in this textbook. A game company entering an unrelated agricultural business illustrates conglomerate diversification. The examples clarify the relationship rather than asserting facts about a real company. The textbook’s inquiry on page 215 repeats the word conglomerate in a prompt whose description matches concentric. Use the definitions on page 214 to resolve that printing inconsistency. In a response, justify the category by the change being made.
table: Existing service adapted for business users
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 214–215.

slides.title: Hiring systems affect opportunity
lines: A system can screen applicants quickly
Historical labels can preserve past exclusion
A relevant measure and a challenge route need evaluation
slides.notes: The chapter discusses automated hiring and psychometric testing as historical examples. A psychometric survey aims to measure capabilities or behavioural characteristics. A screening system may reduce processing time, but its measures must relate to the role and work appropriately for different applicants. We do not treat the textbook’s descriptions of named vendors in 2022 as their current product specifications. For an inquiry, verify present practices and examine the evidence for validity, accessibility and unequal outcomes.

quiz.q: What most directly links hiring to algorithmic dilemmas?
options: The appearance of an application page
The choice of data, labels and screening criteria
The fact that all firms use identical software
quiz.why: These decisions can influence whose application is advanced or rejected.

slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 215–217.

slides.title: A historical case needs a current check
lines: Textbook examples establish the chapter’s original discussion
Current product details need a current primary source
The underlying dilemma can remain relevant after a product changes
slides.notes: An older account of facial or voice analysis cannot establish what a hiring service offers today. We can still learn from its dilemma: whether a measured signal validly supports a consequential employment decision. Label the date, separate the general idea from the vendor claim, and seek current documentation before writing a present-tense case. Our required real cases this week use the dated provider, regulator, YouTube and ILO sources in the case file. This prevents a vivid historical example from becoming an unsupported current assertion.
slides.prompt: Rewrite a historical product claim so its date and limit remain clear.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 216–217.

slides.title: Working practices and office design
lines: Digital tasks can change where and how work happens
Office design can support collaboration or quiet work
A flexible environment does not guarantee good working conditions
slides.notes: The textbook describes start-ups, office design and digital working practices. A start-up is an organization in an early stage of development. Funding and product uncertainty can affect workers. Flexible spaces and shared tools can support coordination, yet open rooms can also distract people and some tasks need privacy. The historical descriptions of particular company offices are not current evidence of employee experience. Judge the arrangement against the task and the people who use it, including access, concentration and boundaries between work and personal time.
slides.prompt: Which task benefits from a shared space? Which needs a quiet or private space?
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 217.

slides.title: Remote work and digital nomadism
lines: Remote work uses networks to complete work away from a central workplace
A digital nomad works remotely while moving between locations
Connectivity, access and security can constrain that flexibility
slides.notes: An employee working from home can be remote without being a digital nomad. A person travelling while completing online work may be both. The system requires suitable devices, networks, access to files and ways to coordinate. That can expand location choices, but time zones, unreliable access and data handling can introduce costs. Permission to work across borders depends on the specific setting, so a course discussion should investigate the relevant rules rather than assume freedom to work anywhere.
slides.prompt: Both people work remotely. What makes the travel setting different? Explain one network dependency.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 217–218.
slides.alt: Conceptual AI split scene: a worker at home and a worker at a travel location connect laptops to a shared server. Both work remotely.

slides.title: Crowdsourcing and crowdfunding
lines: Crowdsourcing gathers contributions, information or work
Crowdfunding gathers money for a project or cause
Both need decisions about participation and use
slides.notes: A group asking people to submit designs is crowdsourcing. A group asking for donations to produce an exhibition is crowdfunding. One gathers contributions of work or information, and the other gathers money. A crowdsourced collection may contain errors or uneven perspectives, so someone still needs to evaluate it. Crowdfunding does not guarantee a project will succeed. Use a specific example and identify what is being contributed. No account creation, payment or participation in a labour platform is required for this lesson.

quiz.q: A class requests volunteer translations of its event guide. What is being gathered?
quiz.why: The contribution is work. Its quality and representation still need checking.

slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 218–219.

slides.title: Microwork, gig work and sharing
lines: Microwork consists of small tasks completed for payment
Gig platforms match short-term service providers and customers
Sharing arrangements provide access to assets or services
slides.notes: These categories can overlap, but they emphasize different features. Labelling individual images for payment is microwork. A platform matching a customer with someone to complete a delivery illustrates gig work. Renting access to equipment through a booking service illustrates a sharing arrangement. A creator earning advertising revenue is not automatically performing microwork. Explain the task, payment arrangement and platform’s role before drawing comparisons. Avoid assuming the same working conditions across all digital work.
slides.prompt: Classify an invented paid image-labelling task and an equipment rental. Explain the distinction.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 219.
slides.alt: Teaching diagram: Microwork, gig work and sharing. Its relationships are explained in the visible transcript.

slides.title: Platforms can mediate access to work
lines: A platform can match a worker and a customer
Ratings and allocation rules can influence future access
Workers may have limited information or control
slides.notes: A matching platform reduces the effort needed to find a customer. It may also set the conditions under which a worker appears, receives a task or challenges a rating. That changes the power relationship. A numerical rating can affect visibility without revealing the context of a complaint. These are mechanisms to investigate in a specific case rather than universal findings about every platform. Trace the information that enters the allocation and identify who can change a record or contest the result.
slides.prompt: Identify an opportunity for the worker and a point where the platform exercises power.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 217–219.
slides.alt: Teaching diagram: Platforms can mediate access to work. Its relationships are explained in the visible transcript.

slides.title: Employee organizations and bargaining power
lines: Workers can organize to seek better conditions
Collective bargaining represents a group in negotiation
A worker’s status and rights depend on the actual arrangement
slides.notes: The textbook explains employee organizations and collective bargaining, and raises the contrast between employment and contracted task provision. Digital coordination can help workers share information and organize. The applicable rights and benefits depend on law and the actual relationship in a particular jurisdiction. We will not label every gig worker the same way. An inquiry needs a defined place, period and source. The conceptual question is how the platform’s control and the worker’s ability to negotiate affect the distribution of benefits and risks.
slides.prompt: What evidence would you need before comparing a platform employee with a contracted worker?
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 219.

slides.title: Real source Y: revenue share and creator income
lines: YouTube describes different payment bases for Watch Page and Shorts
A revenue-share rate needs its denominator
A share rate alone does not establish a creator’s income
slides.notes: The provider’s earnings overview specifies a Watch Page share of 55 percent of net advertising revenue and a Shorts share of 45 percent of the revenue allocated from the Creator Pool. Those denominators differ. Comparing the percentages alone does not show which gives a particular creator more income. Income also depends on the eligible revenue, allocation and activity. Use the exact terms and source locator in the case file. This source supports the stated payment rules, not an independent finding about earnings stability.

quiz.q: Why can’t we compare 55% and 45% as if they were the same payment?
options: The larger number guarantees higher income
quiz.why: The denominator and allocated amount are essential to the comparison.

slides.source_note: YouTube Partner earnings overview, checked 5 October 2026. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72902 Textbook connection: pp. 213–219.

slides.title: Real source L: opportunities and working conditions
lines: The ILO examines different forms of platform work
Its 2021 evidence is useful for historical context
It cannot establish a current TikTok creator’s earnings
slides.notes: The ILO’s historical research summary considers platform work from a labour perspective. It helps us ask about access to work, working conditions and social protection. Its date and scope matter. Use it to frame a labour question and compare with an appropriate current case, not to calculate a creator’s present income. A source may be relevant to one part of an inquiry and insufficient for another. That is why the source passport ties usefulness to a specific claim.
slides.prompt: Which part of a creator-income inquiry could this source inform? What evidence is still needed?
slides.source_note: ILO, 23 February 2021, historical research summary. https://www.ilo.org/resource/news/rapid-growth-digital-economy-calls-coherent-policy-response-0 Textbook connection: pp. 217–219.

slides.title: An impact becomes an implication through a reasoned link
lines: Mechanism: a rule changes visibility
Impact: a named group receives a changed opportunity
Implication: the longer-term significance depends on evidence and conditions
slides.notes: Consider our invented museum feed. A discovery weight increases exposure for an unfamiliar topic. A possible immediate impact is that a new creator gains opportunities to be seen. A possible implication is a broader range of creators sustaining an audience, but that requires continued exposure and suitable income opportunities. The implication is not simply a more dramatic synonym for the impact. State the time horizon, the affected group and the conditions linking them. Your Friday response uses real evidence and must retain the limits of those sources.
slides.prompt: Build a different chain for a worker allocated fewer paid tasks. State one condition.
slides.source_note: Bomfim et al., Digital Society for the IB Diploma, Hodder, 2022. Printed pages cited per slide. Original paraphrase. Textbook connection: pp. 213–219.

Identify the one distinction you still need to revisit.

Explicit teaching, guided application, independent transfer and later retrieval
